q: The person who prohibits halaal is the same as the one who permits haraam. Prohibiting halaal is as sinful as permitting haraam.
It is Sunnat to walk one’s guest to the door of the house.
Beware of assumptions, for statements based upon them are most likely to be untruthful.
Barakat lies with your elders.
The cowardly businessman goes unrewarded, while the one who is courageous is rewarded with his livelihood.

In the zill (shade) of the ‘arsh (Throne), on the day there is no other zill, will be the man who leaves his home to trade and seek sustenance from Allah Ta‘ala’s grace. He does this to prevent himself from asking of others and to provide for his family.
Planning is one half of life. Proper planning is essential for a fulfilling life.
Exchange gifts with one another for doing so increases affection and cleanses hearts of grudges and ill will.

Three people remain untouched by the trials and tribulations of this world and the hereafter:
• the person who offers sincere advice to Muslims,
• the person who guides towards good,
• the person who is content with Allah Ta‘ala’s judgement and will.
Having a sense of shame is goodness in its entirety.
All Creation is a family dependent on Allah Ta‘ala. The most beloved of all Creation to Him, therefore, is the one who benefits His family the most.
Du‘aa’ is a Mumin’s weapon.
The person who provides water should be the last to drink.
Greet your family with salaam and the well-being of your home will greatly increase.
When you meet someone from my Ummah, greet him with salaam and your hasanaat will greatly increase.
The worst of all earnings are earnings from interest.
Sadaqah given in secret extinguishes Allah Ta‘ala’s anger.
The reward of a person who is thankful for what he eats is similar to that of one who endures his rozah.
Seeking knowledge is obligatory upon every Muslim man and woman.
I am amazed by a person who laughs very loudly, and all the while he is unaware of whether he has pleased Allah Ta‘ala or angered Him.
I am amazed by a person who desires worldly pleasures and all the while Death seeks him.

Knowledge is a Mumin’s companion, Forbearance — together with Sagacity — is his vizier, Intellect is his guide, Action is his leader, Competence is his father, Kindness is his brother and Endurance is the commander of his armies.
Al-Quran itself is the cure and du‘aa’ itself is ‘ibaadat.
Speak al-Haq (what is true and right) even though it may be bitter.
The betrayal is great when your brother believes you to be truthful about what you tell him [because it comes from you], and all along you are lying.
The honour of a home lies in sweeping it (keeping it clean).
The honour of a garment lies in folding it properly.
Do not speak ill of Muslims behind their backs nor pursue their flaws.
Do not sleep unless you are in a state of tahaarat, for if you pass away [while sleeping in a state of tahaarat] you will die a shaheed.
Do not make a promise to your brother that you will not keep.
Not a single one of you should ever wish for death as a result of a hardship that has befallen him.
A Muslim is not permitted to sever relations with his brother for more than three days.

A man will not perfect his belief in Allah Ta‘ala without five qualities:
• having faith in Allah Ta‘ala,
• entrusting all matters to Him,
• submitting to His command,
• accepting His judgement gladly,
• enduring His trials.
A Mumin will not be bitten twice in the same snake nest. A Mumin will stay away from what has harmed him once before.
A powerful person is not one who brings another to the ground. Truly powerful is he who controls himself when angry.
A wealthy person is not one who has an abundance of material possessions. Truly wealthy is he who is content with whatever he has and is not dependent on anyone.
A youth will not show deference to an elder out of consideration for his age, but Allah Ta‘ala will provide him with someone who will show him deference when he reaches that age as well.
A man does not open for himself the door that leads to begging, but Allah Ta‘ala opens for him the door that leads to poverty.
No act of Allah Ta‘ala’s taa‘at (obedience) is rewarded more swiftly than the act of ensuring good relations with one’s family and relatives.
A father has not given his child a better gift than good manners.
A vile companion is like a blacksmith fanning a fire with his bellows: even if he does not burn you with the sparks of his fire, his odour will certainly stay with you.
A virtuous companion is like a merchant of Dari musk: even if he does not offer you his perfume, his fragrance will certainly linger with you.
A Mumin is like a honeybee: it does not consume nor give except that which is pure and wholesome.
He whose advice is sought is considered to be trustworthy. Therefore, it is his responsibility to give reliable, honest advice.
A Muslim is one from whose words and actions other Muslims remain unharmed.
If a person wishes to be the wealthiest of all people, he should rely more on what is in Allah Ta‘ala’s hands than what is in his own.
If a person builds a masjid for Allah Ta‘ala, even if like the nest of a sandgrouse, Allah Ta‘ala will build for him a home in jannat.
He who humbles himself before Allah Ta‘ala, Allah Ta‘ala will raise him.
The merit of a man’s Islam is in disregarding matters that do not concern him.
If a person has been provided a means by which he has obtained his livelihood, he should remain committed to it.
He who conceals his brother’s faults, Allah Ta‘ala will conceal his faults in this world and the hereafter.
Good character is part of a man’s good fortune.
Allah Ta‘ala takes responsibility for the livelihood of one who seeks knowledge.
When a door leading to good opens for someone, he should promptly seize the opportunity for he does not know when that door will close.
A person slain while defending his family is a shaheed (martyr) as is a person slain while defending his faith.
A person slain while defending his wealth is a shaheed as is a person slain while defending himself.
He who believes in Allah Ta‘ala and the Last Day (Day of Qiyaamat) should speak that which is good or remain silent.
He who believes in Allah Ta‘ala and the Last Day should honour and respect his neighbour.
He who believes in Allah Ta‘ala and the Last Day should honour and be hospitable to his guests.
When a person controls his anger despite being able to express it, Allah Ta‘ala infuses his heart with peace and faith.
Among the treasures of goodness is the concealment of hardships, illnesses and sadaqah.
He who is not thankful for a little will not be thankful for a lot.
When one of you walks towards a meal, he should walk slowly and unhurriedly.
If a person helps his brother without his knowing, Allah Ta‘ala will help him in this world and the hereafter.
If a person looks at his brother with the intent of finding fault, Allah Ta‘ala will regard him with anger in this world and the hereafter.

If a person looks at a Mumin in a manner that frightens him, Allah Ta‘ala will fill him with fear on the Day there is no zill but His. He will bring him forth in the form of an ant — with his flesh, body, and all his limbs and organs — until he is brought to where he belongs.
He, who looks through his brother’s books [letters or any other text] without his permission, is as if he looks at hellfire.
A Mumin is a Mumin’s brother; he neither wrongs him nor insults him.
A Mumin for another Mumin is like a structure whose various parts support one another. Like the parts of a structure, one Mumin supports and strengthens another.
Allah Ta‘ala’s gift to a Mumin is someone in need at his door.
One of you notices a speck of straw in his brother’s eye but ignores the trunk of a date palm in his own. He notices the smallest imperfections of others but ignores significant ones in himself.
Patience is the grave of all flaws. Through patience and self-restraint, one’s flaws remain hidden.
Beware of the good-natured man’s assault when he is hungry and that of the vile man after he has eaten his fill.
Show kindness to others’ children and you will remain protected in yours. Your children will be shown kindness as well.
Ward off the waves of hardship with du‘aa’.
When generosity is shown to you, repay it with an act of greater generosity. Nevertheless, the distinction remains with the one who acted first.
When you become impoverished, engage in trade with Allah Ta‘ala by giving sadaqah (by giving zakaat wholeheartedly).
When the intellect matures, words decrease.
When a Mumin expresses irritation or displeasure with his brother by uttering “uff” to him, their bond of affection is broken.

When you seek something from Allah Ta‘ala, begin your request by asking Him to pray salawaat upon Rasulullah (SA) and then ask for what you seek. When two things are asked of Him together, Allah Ta‘ala is too honourable to fulfill one and deny the other.
You have three friends and three enemies. Your friends are: your friend, your friend’s friend and your enemy’s enemy. Your enemies are: your enemy, your friend’s enemy and your enemy’s friend.
Gratefully acknowledge Allah Ta‘ala in times of comfort and ease, and He will acknowledge you [with aid and assistance] in times of difficulty.
Poverty is undoubtedly a hardship, but a more severe hardship than poverty is illness of the body. And an even more severe hardship than illness of the body is illness of the soul.

A father has a responsibility towards his son and a son has a duty towards his father. A son’s duty towards his father is that he obeys him in all matters other than in the disobedience of Allah Subhaanahu. A father’s responsibility towards his son is that [in accordance with the guidance of Awliyaullah (SA)] he names him well, ensures that he is well mannered and teaches him al-Quran.

There is little value in [a person’s] knowledge when it is limited to the tongue (to words). The most valuable knowledge is that which manifests itself in the limbs and parts of the body (in actions).
Stinginess encompasses all the worst flaws and is the reins by which one is led towards every evil.
What an awful preparation for the journey to the hereafter is injustice towards other men!

Protect yourselves at the onset of the cold season and embrace it at its end for the cold has the same effect on bodies that it has on trees. The arrival of the cold season burns trees [causing their leaves to fall] but the end revives them [with fresh leaves].
To praise more than what is deserved is flattery. To praise insufficiently, on the other hand, is either due to an inability to express oneself or jealousy.
Anger is a type of madness because a person who succumbs to his anger shows remorse later on. However, if he shows no remorse then [understand that] his madness still continues.
Food that has gone sour is preferable to sour words.
Fear Allah Ta‘ala and you will be safe from all others.
Always control your anger and the outcomes [of your endeavours] will be praiseworthy.
Lasting happiness lies in seeing [one’s] brothers.

A person who approves of a certain group’s act is the same as the one who participates in that act with them. And when participating in an act that is Baatil (wrongful), a person commits two sins: the sin of carrying it out and the sin of approval.
Your livelihood seeks you so be at ease. Have faith in Allah Ta‘ala and do not be anxious.
The beauty of that which is hidden is greater than the beauty of that which is apparent.
A person who listens to backbiting is himself one of those who backbite.
Generosity is giving before being asked. As for giving after being asked, it is either out of shame or fear of being criticised.

When asked about Allah Ta‘ala’s words, “We will most certainly endow him with a life of hayaat tayyibah (a life that is good and pure)”, Amirul Mumineen (SA) replied that it (hayaat tayyibah) is contentment.
The condition of friendship is doing away with formalities.
The heart’s cure is the recitation of al-Quran.
A wise man’s chest is the chest of his secrets.
[When you need to] Rebuke your brother [do so] by being generous to him and turn away his ill will with an act of kindness towards him.
A wise man is one who is advised by experience.
A man’s self-admiration is one among those who are jealous of his intellect. Those jealous of an intelligent person wish for the ruin of his intellect.
I gained ma‘rifah of Allah through the breaking down of firm determination and the unravelling of strong resolve.
You are obliged to make an effort, but you are not obliged to succeed. Success is in the hands of Allah Ta‘ala.
The doer of good is better than the good he does while the doer of evil is worse than the evil he commits.
A man’s liberation is in the truth.
Failing to achieve a desire is easier [to bear] than seeking it from people who are unfit to be asked.

While responding to a question put forward to him about what was greater than the universe, Amirul Mumineen (AS) stated that it was slander. That is when a Mumin makes false and malicious statements about another Mumin.
When asked to describe a sensible man, Amirul Mumineen (SA) replied, “He is the one who places each thing where it belongs.” He was then asked to describe a fool to which he answered, “I just did.”
Amirul Mumineen (AS) was asked, “If a man was to be locked up in a house and left there, how would his livelihood come to him?” He replied, “In the very same way his death would.”
Each man’s worth is [determined by] what he does well.
Some morsels are such that they prevent many more.
Generosity is complete when accompanied by an apology [that one has not given enough].
Do not complain about your illness [to anyone] except to the one who can provide you with a cure.
Never think ill of another’s remarks when it is possible for you to find some good in them.
There can be no closeness [to Allah Ta‘ala] in doing good deeds that are not obligated if they harm those that are.
People will not neglect an aspect of their religion in order to deal with a worldly concern, but Allah Ta‘ala will bring upon them something that is far worse.

The fulfillment of needs will not be proper without three conditions. [When fulfilling the needs of others, one should:]
• Consider them insignificant and their importance will increase.
• Be discreet about them and they will become known.
• Attend to them promptly and they will be beneficial.
A man cannot be faulted for a delay in receiving what is rightfully his. He is at fault, however, for taking what is not rightfully his.
A friend is not a friend unless he protects his brother in three situations: in his difficulty, in his absence and in his death.

A Mumin should divide his time into three parts:
• a time for worship and devotion to Allah Ta‘ala,
• a time for attending to his livelihood,
• a time for pursuing pleasures that are halaal and appropriate.
Nothing is [considered to be] lost from your wealth if it has taught you a lesson.
Speak gently and you will be loved.
A person does not confine something to his thoughts but it escapes through slips of his tongue and expressions of his face.
The person suffering from severe hardship is no more in need of du‘aa’ than one free from it; [for] he, too, is not safe from its reach. Du‘aa’ is always necessary.
A martyr in Allah Ta‘ala’s cause is no more deserving of reward than a person who though capable of carrying out an immoral act, refrains from it. Indeed, such a person is nearly a firishtah.
Anything [deemed to be] good is not good if it leads to hellfire. And anything [deemed to be] evil is not evil if it leads to jannat.
Associating oneself with [a group of] people in their character and behaviour offers protection from their malice.
He who is obstinate will perish.
When a person mends that which is between himself and Allah Ta‘ala, Allah Ta‘ala will mend that which is between him and others.
If a Mumin saves his brother from hunger, Allah Ta‘ala will provide him with the fruits of jannat.
He who is mindful of the journey’s distance prepares [for it].
The person who warns you is like the one who brings you glad tidings.
He who draws the sword of tyranny, will himself be killed by it.
When a person considers small hardships to be great, Allah Ta‘ala will bring upon him hardships that are [in fact] great.
An ungrateful person will not achieve success.
When one’s own soul (conscience) is his advisor, Allah Ta‘ala is his protector.

When a person talks too much, his mistakes increase.
When one’s mistakes increase, his sense of shame diminishes.
When one’s sense of shame diminishes, he is less inclined to refrain from sin.
When one is less inclined to refrain from sin, his heart (conscience) dies.
A person whose heart is dead will enter hellfire.
The atonement for grave sins is in giving succour to the oppressed and in providing relief to the distressed.
A person should never blame another for suspecting him of doing wrong if he places himself in positions in which he is vulnerable to accusation.
People are enemies of what they do not know.
Bring forth what you possess, for through it, you will be known.
Running away from your own self (self-indulgence) is more beneficial than running away from a lion.
O son of Adam! When you perceive that Allah Ta‘ala continues to bestow His bounties upon you and all the while you disobey Him, fear Him.
A person who informs on others with malicious intent creates a month’s worth of discord in an instant.
The deed dearest to Allah Ta‘ala is that which is most consistent, even if small.
When someone distinguished from a community visits you, honour him.
Gladly accept Allah Ta‘ala’s will and you will [truly] become a zaahid.
Perfect your wudu’ and you will live longer.
Completing an act of kindness is better than starting it. If you start an act of kindness, complete it.
Seek help in the fulfillment of [your] needs by concealing them.
Do good to the worthy and the unworthy. If a person is worthy, then he is deserving of that good. If a person is unworthy, then you are one who does good regardless.
The bane of generosity is extravagance.
The bane of speech is lying.
The bane of nobility is to be overproud.
The bane of forbearance is foolishness.
The bane of munificence is recounting favours.
The bane of courage is oppression. Courage should not lead one to transgress the limits of what is just and right.
The bane of cleverness is conceitedness.
The bane of ‘ibaadat is listlessness.
The bane of knowledge is to forget.
Enquire about your neighbour before purchasing a house and about your companion before embarking upon a journey.
The dictation of good is better than silence. However, silence is better than the dictation of evil.
What most entitles people to enter jannat is the taqwaa of Allah Ta‘ala and good character.
Jealousy consumes hasanaat (good deeds) the way fire consumes wood.
Through the goodness of his character, a man attains the status of one dedicated to rozah and namaaz.

In all His justice and fairness, Allah Ta‘ala has determined that comfort and relief shall reside in faith and contentment. Likewise, He has determined that worry and sorrow shall reside in doubt and discontentment.
When the intention [behind a deed] is to obtain aakherat, Allah Ta‘ala grants dunyaa [along with aakherat]. However, when the intention is worldly, He refuses to grant aakherat.
A small number of deeds undertaken with knowledge and understanding amounts to a lot. However, a large number of deeds carried out in ignorance and without understanding amounts to little.
a: إِنَّ مُحَرِّمَ الْحَلَالِ كَمُحِلِّ الْحَرَامِ

إِنَّ مِنَ السُّنَّةِ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ الرَّجُلُ مَعَ ضَيْفِهِ
إِلَى بَابِ الدَّارِ
إِيَّاكُمْ وَالظَّنَّ فَإِنَّ الظَّنَّ أَكْذَبُ الْحَدِيثِ
الْبَرَكَةُ مَعَ أَكَابِرِكُمْ

التَّاجِرُ الْجَبَانُ مَحْرُومٌ
وَالتَّاجِرُ الْجَسُورُ مَرْزُوقٌ

تَحْتَ ظِلِّ الْعَرْشِ يَوْمَ لَا ظِلَّ إِلَّا ظِلُّهُ
رَجُلٌ خَرَجَ ضَارِبًا فِي الْأَرْضِ يَطْلُبُ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللهِ
مَا يَكُفُّ بِهِ نَفْسَهُ وَيَعُودُ بِهِ عَلَى عِيَالِهِ
التَّدْبِيرُ نِصْفُ الْعَيْشِ

تَهَادَوْا فَإِنَّهُ يُضَعِّفُ الْحُبَّ
وَيَذْهَبُ بِغَوَائِلِ الصُّدُورِ

ثَلَاثَةٌ لَا تَمَسُّهُمْ فِتْنَةُ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
مَنْ نَصَحَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
وَمَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى الْخَيْرِ
وَمَنْ رَضِيَ بِقَضَاءِ اللهِ وَقَدَرِهِ
الْحَيَاءُ خَيْرٌ كُلُّهُ

الْخَلْقُ كُلُّهُمْ عِيَالُ اللهِ
فَأَحَبُّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ أَنْفَعُهُمْ لِعِيَالِهِ
الدُّعَاءُ سِلَاحُ الْمُؤْمِنِ
سَاقِي الْقَوْمِ آخِرُهُمْ شُرْبًا
سَلِّمْ عَلَى أَهْلِ بَيْتِكَ يَكْثُرْ خَيْرُ بَيْتِكَ
سَلِّمْ عَلَى مَنْ لَقِيتَ مِنْ أُمَّتِي تَكْثُرْ حَسَنَاتُكَ
شَرُّ الْمَكَاسِبِ كَسْبُ الرِّبَا
صَدَقَةُ السِّرِّ تُطْفِئُ غَضَبَ الرَّبِّ
الطَّاعِمُ الشَّاكِرُ لَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ الصَّائِمِ الصَّابِرِ
طَلَبُ الْعِلْمِ فَرِيضَةٌ عَلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ وَمُسْلِمَةٍ

عَجِبْتُ لِضَاحِكٍ مِلْءَ فِيهِ
وَلَا يَدْرِي أَرَضِيَ اللهُ أَمْ أَسْخَطَهُ
عَجِبْتُ لِمُؤَمِّلٍ دُنْيَا وَالْمَوْتُ يَطْلُبُهُ

الْعِلْمُ خَلِيلُ الْمُؤْمِنِ
وَالْحِلْمُ وَزِيرُهُ وَالْعَقْلُ دَلِيلُهُ
وَالْعَمَلُ قَائِدُهُ وَالرِّفْقُ وَالِدُهُ
وَالْبِرُّ أَخُوهُ وَالصَّبْرُ أَمِيرُ جُنُودِهِ
الْقُرْآنُ هُوَ الدَّوَاءُ وَالدُّعَاءُ هُوَ الْعِبَادَةُ
قُلِ الْحَقَّ وَإِنْ كَانَ مُرًّا

كَبُرَتْ خِيَانَةً أَنْ تُحَدِّثَ أَخَاكَ حَدِيثًا
هُوَ لَكَ بِهِ مُصَدِّقٌ وَأَنْتَ لَهُ كَاذِبٌ
كَرَمُ الْبَيْتِ كَنْسُهُ
كَرَمُ الثَّوْبِ طَيُّهُ
لَا تَغْتَابُوا الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا عَوْرَاتِهِمْ

لَا تَنَمْ إِلَّا وَأَنْتَ طَاهِرٌ
فَإِنَّكَ إِنْ مُتَّ مُتَّ شَهِيدًا
لَا تُوَاعِدْ أَخَاكَ مَوْعِدًا فَتُخْلِفَهُ
لَا يَتَمَنَّيَنَّ أَحَدُكُمُ الْمَوْتَ لِضُرٍّ نَزَلَ بِهِ
لَا يَحِلُّ لِمُسْلِمٍ أَنْ يَهْجُرَ أَخَاهُ فَوْقَ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ

لَا يَكْمُلُ الْعَبْدُ الْإِيمَانَ بِاللهِ
حَتَّى تَكُونَ فِيهِ خَمْسُ خِصَالٍ
التَّوَكُّلُ عَلَى اللهِ وَالتَّفْوِيضُ إِلَى اللهِ
وَالتَّسْلِيمُ لِأَمْرِ اللهِ وَالرِّضَى بِقَضَاءِ اللهِ
وَالصَّبْرُ عَلَى بَلَاءِ اللهِ
لَا يُلْدَغُ الْمُؤْمِنُ فِي جُحْرٍ وَاحِدٍ مَرَّتَيْنِ

لَيْسَ الشَّدِيدُ بِالصُّرَعَةِ
إِنَّمَا الشَّدِيدُ الَّذِي يَمْلِكُ نَفْسَهُ
عِنْدَ الْغَضَبِ

لَيْسَ الْغِنَى عَنْ كَثْرَةِ الْعَرَضِ
إِنَّمَا الْغِنَى غِنَى النَّفْسِ

مَا أَكْرَمَ شَابٌّ شَيْخًا لِسِنِّهِ
إِلَّا قَيَّضَ اللهُ لَهُ عِنْدَ سِنِّهِ مَنْ يُكْرِمُهُ

مَا فَتَحَ رَجُلٌ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ بَابَ مَسْأَلَةٍ
إِلَّا فَتَحَ اللهُ عَلَيْهِ بَابَ فَقْرٍ

مَا مِنْ شَيْءٍ أُطِيعَ اللهُ فِيهِ
بِأَعْجَلَ ثَوَابًا مِنْ صِلَةِ الرَّحِمِ
مَا نَحَلَ وَالِدٌ وَلَدَهُ أَفْضَلَ مِنْ أَدَبٍ حَسَنٍ

مَثَلُ الْجَلِيسِ السُّوءِ مَثَلُ صَاحِبِ الْكِيرِ
إِنْ لَمْ يُحْرِقْكَ مِنْ شَرَارِ نَارِهِ
عَلِقَكَ مِنْ نَتْنِهِ

مَثَلُ الْجَلِيسِ الصَّالِحِ مَثَلُ الدَّارِيِّ
إِنْ لَمْ يُحْذِكَ مِنْ عِطْرِهِ عَلِقَكَ مِنْ رِيحِهِ

مَثَلُ الْمُؤْمِنِ كَمَثَلِ النَّحْلَةِ
لَا تَأْكُلُ إِلَّا طَيِّبًا وَلَا تَضَعُ إِلَّا طَيِّبًا
الْمُسْتَشَارُ مُؤْتَمَنٌ
الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ يَدِهِ وَلِسَانِهِ

مَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ أَغْنَى النَّاسِ
فَلْيَكُنْ بِمَا فِي يَدِ اللهِ أَوْثَقَ مِنْهُ بِمَا فِي يَدِهِ

مَنْ بَنَى للهِ مَسْجِدًا وَلَوْ مِثْلَ مَفْحَصِ قَطَاةٍ
بَنَى اللهُ لَهُ بَيْتًا فِي الْجَنَّةِ
مَنْ تَوَاضَعَ للهِ رَفَعَهُ اللهُ
مِنْ حُسْنِ إِسْلَامِ الْمَرْءِ تَرْكُهُ مَا لَا يَعْنِيهِ
مَنْ رُزِقَ بِشَيْءٍ فَلْيَلْزَمْهُ

مَنْ سَتَرَ عَلَى أَخِيهِ
سَتَرَ اللهُ عَلَيْهِ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
مِنْ سَعَادَةِ الْمَرْءِ حُسْنُ الْخُلُقِ
مَنْ طَلَبَ الْعِلْمَ تَكَفَّلَ اللهُ بِرِزْقِهِ

مَنْ فُتِحَ لَهُ بَابُ خَيْرٍ فَلْيَنْتَهِزْهُ
فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَدْرِي مَتَى يُغْلَقُ عَنْهُ

مَنْ قُتِلَ دُونَ أَهْلِهِ فَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ
وَمَنْ قُتِلَ دُونَ دِينِهِ فَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ

مَنْ قُتِلَ دُونَ مَالِهِ فَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ
وَمَنْ قُتِلَ دُونَ نَفْسِهِ فَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ

مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ
فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيُكْرِمْ جَارَهُ
مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيُكْرِمْ ضَيْفَهُ

مَنْ كَظَمَ غَيْظًا وَهُوَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى إِنْفَاذِهِ
مَلَأَ اللهُ قَلْبَهُ أَمْنًا وَإِيمَانًا

مِنْ كُنُوزِ الْبِرِّ
كِتْمَانُ الْمَصَائِبِ وَالْأَمْرَاضِ وَالصَّدَقَةِ
مَنْ لَمْ يَشْكُرِ الْقَلِيلَ لَمْ يَشْكُرِ الْكَثِيرَ
مَنْ مَشَى مِنْكُمْ إِلَى طَعَامٍ فَلْيَمْشِ رُوَيْدًا

مَنْ نَصَرَ أَخَاهُ بِظَهْرِ الْغَيْبِ
نَصَرَهُ اللهُ تَعَالَى فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ

مَنْ نَظَرَ أَخَاهُ بِعَيْنِ عَيْبٍ
نَظَرَهُ اللهُ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ بِعَيْنِ غَضَبٍ

مَنْ نَظَرَ إِلَى مُؤْمِنٍ نَظْرَةً يُخِيفُهُ بِهَا
أَخَافَهُ اللهُ يَوْمَ لَا ظِلَّ إِلَّا ظِلُّهُ
وَحَشَرَهُ فِي صُورَةِ الذَّرَّةِ بِلَحْمِهِ وَجَسَدِهِ
وَجَمِيعِ أَعْضَائِهِ حَتَّى يُورِدَهُ مَوْرِدَهُ

مَنْ نَظَرَ فِي كِتَابِ أَخِيهِ بِغَيْرِ إِذْنِهِ
فَكَأَنَّمَا يَنْظُرُ فِي النَّارِ
الْمُؤْمِنُ أَخُو الْمُؤْمِنِ لَا يَظْلِمُهُ وَلَا يَشْتُمُهُ

الْمُؤْمِنُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ كَالْبُنْيَانِ
يَشُدُّ بَعْضُهُ بَعْضًا
هَدِيَّةُ اللهِ إِلَى الْمُؤْمِنِ السَّائِلُ عَلَى بَابِهِ

يَنْظُرُ أَحَدُكُمُ الْقَذَى فِي عَيْنِ أَخِيهِ
وَيَدَعُ الْجِذْعَ فِي عَيْنِهِ
الِاحْتِمَالُ قَبْرُ الْعُيُوبِ

احْذَرُوا صَوْلَةَ الْكَرِيمِ إِذَا جَاعَ
وَاللَّئِيمِ إِذَا شَبِعَ

أَحْسِنُوا فِي عَقِبِ غَيْرِكُمْ
تُحْفَظُوا فِي عَقِبِكُمْ
ادْفَعُوا أَمْوَاجَ الْبَلَاءِ بِالدُّعَاءِ

إِذَا أُسْدِيَتْ إِلَيْكَ يَدٌ فَكَافِئْهَا بِمَا يُرْبِي عَلَيْهَا
وَالْفَضْلُ مَعَ ذَلِكَ لِلْبَادِي
إِذَا أَمْلَقْتُمْ فَتَاجِرُوا اللهَ بِالصَّدَقَةِ
إِذَا تَمَّ الْعَقْلُ نَقَصَ الْكَلَامُ

إِذَا قَالَ الْمُؤْمِنُ لِأَخِيهِ أُفٍّ انْقَطَعَ
مَا بَيْنَهُمَا مِنَ الْمَوَدَّةِ

إِذَا كَانَتْ لَكَ إِلَى اللهِ حَاجَةٌ
فَابْدَأِ الْمَسْأَلَةَ بِالصَّلَاةِ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ
ثُمَّ سَلْ حَاجَتَكَ
فَإِنَّ اللهَ أَكْرَمُ أَنْ يُسْأَلَ حَاجَتَيْنِ
فَيَقْضِيَ إِحْدَاهُمَا وَيَمْنَعَ الْأُخْرَى

أَصْدِقَاؤُكَ ثَلَاثَةٌ وَأَعْدَاؤُكَ ثَلَاثَةٌ
فَأَصْدِقَاؤُكَ
صَدِيقُكَ، وَصَدِيقُ صَدِيقِكَ، وَعَدُوُّ عَدُوِّكَ
وَأَعْدَاؤُكَ
عَدُوُّكَ، وَعَدُوُّ صَدِيقِكَ، وَصَدِيقُ عَدُوِّكَ

اعْرِفِ اللهَ فِي الرَّخَاءِ
يَعْرِفْكَ فِي الشِّدَّةِ

أَلَا وَإِنَّ مِنَ الْبَلَاءِ الْفَاقَةَ
وَأَشَدُّ مِنَ الْفَاقَةِ مَرَضُ الْبَدَنِ
وَأَشَدُّ مِنْ مَرَضِ الْبَدَنِ مَرَضُ الْقَلْبِ

إِنَّ لِلْوَلَدِ عَلَى الْوَالِدِ حَقًّا
وَإِنَّ لِلْوَالِدِ عَلَى الْوَلَدِ حَقًّا
فَحَقُّ الْوَالِدِ عَلَى الْوَلَدِ
أَنْ يُطِيعَهُ فِي كُلِّ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا فِي مَعْصِيَةِ اللهِ سُبْحَانَهُ
وَحَقُّ الْوَلَدِ عَلَى الْوَالِدِ
أَنْ يُحْسِنَ اسْمَهُ وَيُحْسِنَ أَدَبَهُ وَيُعَلِّمَهُ الْقُرْآنَ

أَوْضَعُ الْعِلْمِ مَا وَقَفَ عَلَى اللِّسَانِ
وَأَرْفَعُهُ مَا ظَهَرَ عَلَى الْجَوَارِحِ وَالْأَرْكَانِ
بِالْإِخْلَاصِ يَكُونُ الْخَلَاصُ

بِئْسَ الزَّادُ إِلَى الْمَعَادِ
الْعُدْوَانُ عَلَى الْعِبَادِ

تَوَقَّوُا الْبَرْدَ فِي أَوَّلِهِ وَتَلَقَّوْهُ فِي آخِرِهِ
فَإِنَّهُ يَعْمَلُ فِي الْأَبْدَانِ كَمَا يَفْعَلُ فِي الْأَشْجَارِ
أَوَّلُهُ يُحْرِقُ وَآخِرُهُ يُورِقُ

الثَّنَاءُ بِأَكْثَرَ مِنَ الِاسْتِحْقَاقِ مَلَقٌ
وَالتَّقْصِيرُ عَنِ الِاسْتِحْقَاقِ عِيٌّ أَوْ حَسَدٌ

الْحِدَّةُ ضَرْبٌ مِنَ الْجُنُونِ
لِأَنَّ صَاحِبَهَا يَنْدَمُ
فَإِنْ لَمْ يَنْدَمْ فَجُنُونُهُ مُسْتَحْكِمٌ

حُمُوضَاتُ الطَّعَامِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ
حُمُوضَاتِ الْكَلَامِ
خَفِ اللهَ تَأْمَنْ مِنْ غَيْرِهِ
دُمْ عَلَى كَظْمِ الْغَيْظِ تَحْمَدْ عَوَاقِبَكَ
دَوَامُ السُّرُورِ رُؤْيَةُ الْإِخْوَانِ
رِزْقُكَ يَطْلُبُكَ فَاسْتَرِحْ
زِينَةُ الْبَاطِنِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ زِينَةِ الظَّاهِرِ
السَّامِعُ لِلْغِيبَةِ أَحَدُ الْمُغْتَابِينَ

السَّخَاءُ مَا كَانَ ابْتِدَاءً
فَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ عَنْ مَسْأَلَةٍ فَحَيَاءٌ أَوْ تَذَمُّمٌ

سُئِلَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَنْ قَوْلِ اللهِ تَعَالَى
«فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ حَيَاةً طَيِّبَةً»
فَقَالَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ هِيَ الْقَنَاعَةُ
شَرْطُ الْأُلْفَةِ تَرْكُ الْكُلْفَةِ
شِفَاءُ الْجَنَانِ قِرَاءَةُ الْقُرْآنِ
صَدْرُ الْعَاقِلِ صُنْدُوقُ سِرِّهِ

عَاتِبْ أَخَاكَ بِالْإِحْسَانِ إِلَيْهِ
وَارْدُدْ شَرَّهُ بِالْإِنْعَامِ عَلَيْهِ
الْعَاقِلُ مَنْ وَعَظَتْهُ التَّجَارِبُ
عُجْبُ الْمَرْءِ بِنَفْسِهِ أَحَدُ حُسَّادِ عَقْلِهِ

عَرَفْتُ اللهَ سُبْحَانَهُ بِفَسْخِ الْعَزَائِمِ
وَحَلِّ الْعُقُودِ
عَلَيْكَ بِالسَّعْيِ وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ بِالنُّجْحِ
فَاعِلُ الْخَيْرِ خَيْرٌ مِنْهُ وَفَاعِلُ الشَّرِّ شَرٌّ مِنْهُ
فَكَاكُ الْمَرْءِ فِي الصِّدْقِ
فَوْتُ الْحَاجَةِ أَهْوَنُ مِنْ طَلَبِهَا إِلَى غَيْرِ أَهْلِهَا

قَالَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ لِسَائِلٍ سَأَلَهُ
مَا أَكْبَرُ مِنَ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ
قَالَ الْبُهْتُ
وَهُوَ أَنْ يَبْهَتَ الْمُؤْمِنَ مُؤْمِنًا بِمَا لَيْسَ عِنْدَهُ

قِيلَ لَهُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ صِفْ لَنَا الْعَاقِلَ
فَقَالَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ هُوَ الَّذِي يَضَعُ الشَّيْءَ مَوَاضِعَهُ
فَقِيلَ لَهُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ صِفْ لَنَا الْجَاهِلَ
فَقَالَ قَدْ فَعَلْتُ

قِيلَ لَهُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ
لَوْ سُدَّ عَلَى رَجُلٍ بَابُ بَيْتٍ وَتُرِكَ فِيهِ
مِنْ أَيْنَ كَانَ يَأْتِيهِ رِزْقُهُ
فَقَالَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ مِنْ حَيْثُ يَأْتِيهِ أَجَلُهُ
قِيمَةُ كُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا كَانَ يُحْسِنُهُ
كَمْ أَكْلَةٍ مَنَعَتْ أَكَلَاتٍ
كَمَالُ الْجُودِ الِاعْتِذَارُ مَعَهُ
لَا تَشْكُوَنَّ دَاءَكَ إِلَّا عِنْدَ مَنْ عِنْدَهُ دَوَاؤُكَ

لَا تَظُنَّنَّ بِكَلِمَةٍ خَرَجَتْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ سُوءًا
وَأَنْتَ تَجِدُ لَهَا فِي الْخَيْرِ مُحْتَمَلًا
لَا قُرْبَةَ بِالنَّوَافِلِ إِذَا أَضَرَّتْ بِالْفَرَائِضِ

لَا يَتْرُكُ النَّاسُ شَيْئًا مِنْ أَمْرِ دِينِهِمْ
بِاسْتِصْلَاحِ دُنْيَاهُمْ
إِلَّا فَتَحَ اللهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مَا هُوَ أَضَرُّ مِنْهُ

لَا يَسْتَقِيمُ قَضَاءُ الْحَوَائِجِ إِلَّا بِثَلَاثٍ
بِاسْتِصْغَارِهَا لِتَعْظُمَ
وَاسْتِكْتَامِهَا لِتَظْهَرَ
وَتَعْجِيلِهَا لِتَهْنَأَ

لَا يُعَابُ الْمَرْءُ بِتَأْخِيرِ حَقِّهِ
إِنَّمَا يُعَابُ مَنْ أَخَذَ مَا لَيْسَ لَهُ

لَا يَكُونُ الصَّدِيقُ صَدِيقًا
حَتَّى يَحْفَظَ أَخَاهُ فِي ثَلَاثٍ
فِي نَكْبَتِهِ وَغَيْبَتِهِ وَوَفَاتِهِ

لِلْمُؤْمِنِ ثَلَاثُ سَاعَاتٍ
فَسَاعَةٌ فِيهَا يُنَاجِي رَبَّهُ
وَسَاعَةٌ يَرُمُّ فِيهَا مَعَاشَهُ
وَسَاعَةٌ يُخَلِّي بَيْنَ نَفْسِهِ وَبَيْنَ لَذَّتِهَا
فِيمَا يَحِلُّ وَيَجْمُلُ
لَمْ يَذْهَبْ مِنْ مَالِكَ مَا وَعَظَكَ
لِيَنْ قَوْلُكَ تُحْبَبْ

مَا أَضْمَرَ إِنْسَانٌ شَيْئًا
إِلَّا ظَهَرَ فِي فَلَتَاتِ لِسَانِهِ وَصَفَحَاتِ وَجْهِهِ

مَا الْمُبْتَلَى الَّذِي اشْتَدَّ بِهِ الْبَلَاءُ بِأَحْوَجَ
إِلَى الدُّعَاءِ مِنَ الْمُعَافَى الَّذِي لَا يَأْمَنُ الْبَلَاءَ

مَا الْمُجَاهِدُ الشَّهِيدُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللهِ
بِأَعْظَمَ أَجْرًا مِمَّنْ قَدَرَ فَعَفَّ
لَكَادَ الْعَفِيفُ أَنْ يَكُونَ مَلَكًا مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ

مَا خَيْرٌ بِخَيْرٍ بَعْدَهُ النَّارُ
وَمَا شَرٌّ بِشَرٍّ بَعْدَهُ الْجَنَّةُ

مُقَارَبَةُ النَّاسِ فِي أَخْلَاقِهِمْ
أَمْنٌ مِنْ غَوَائِلِهِمْ
مَنِ اسْتَبَدَّ بِرَأْيِهِ هَلَكَ

مَنْ أَصْلَحَ مَا بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ اللهِ
أَصْلَحَ اللهُ مَا بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ النَّاسِ
مَنْ أَطَالَ الْأَمَلَ أَسَاءَ الْعَمَلَ
مَنْ تَذَكَّرَ بُعْدَ السَّفَرِ اسْتَعَدَّ
مَنْ حَذَّرَكَ كَمَنْ بَشَّرَكَ
مَنْ سَلَّ سَيْفَ الْبَغْيِ قُتِلَ بِهِ

مَنْ عَظَّمَ صِغَارَ الْمَصَائِبِ
ابْتَلَاهُ اللهُ بِكِبَارِهَا
مَنْ قَلَّ شُكْرُهُ لَمْ يَنِلِ النُّجْحَ

مَنْ كَانَ لَهُ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ وَاعِظٌ
كَانَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ اللهِ حَافِظٌ

مَنْ كَثُرَ كَلَامُهُ كَثُرَ خَطَاؤُهُ
وَمَنْ كَثُرَ خَطَاؤُهُ قَلَّ حَيَاؤُهُ
وَمَنْ قَلَّ حَيَاؤُهُ قَلَّ وَرَعُهُ
وَمَنْ قَلَّ وَرَعُهُ مَاتَ قَلْبُهُ
وَمَنْ مَاتَ قَلْبُهُ دَخَلَ النَّارَ

مِنْ كَفَّارَاتِ الذُّنُوبِ الْعِظَامِ
إِغَاثَةُ الْمَلْهُوفِ وَالتَّنْفِيسُ عَنِ الْمَكْرُوبِ

مَنْ وَضَعَ نَفْسَهُ مَوَاضِعَ التُّهَمَةِ
فَلَا يَلُومَنَّ مَنْ أَسَاءَ بِهِ ظَنَّهُ
النَّاسُ أَعْدَاءُ مَا جَهِلُوا
هَاتِ مَا عِنْدَكَ تُعْرَفْ بِهِ

هَرَبُكَ مِنْ نَفْسِكَ
أَنْفَعُ مِنْ هَرَبِكَ مِنَ الْأَسَدِ

يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ إِذَا رَأَيْتَ رَبَّكَ سُبْحَانَهُ
يُتَابِعُ عَلَيْكَ نِعَمَهُ وَأَنْتَ تَعْصِيهِ فَاحْذَرْهُ
يَعْمَلُ النَّمَّامُ فِي سَاعَةٍ فِتْنَةَ شَهْرٍ
أَحَبُّ الْأَعْمَالِ إِلَى اللهِ أَدْوَمُهَا وَإِنْ قَلَّ
إِذَا أَتَاكُمْ كَرِيمُ قَوْمٍ فَأَكْرِمُوهُ
ارْضَ بِقِسَمِ اللهِ تَكُنْ زَاهِدًا
أَسْبِغِ الْوُضُوءَ يَزِدْ فِي عُمُرِكَ
اسْتِتْمَامُ الْمَعْرُوفِ خَيْرٌ مِنِ ابْتِدَائِهِ
اسْتَعِينُوا عَلَى نَجَاحِ الْحَوَائِجِ بِالْكِتْمَانِ لَهَا

اصْنَعِ الْمَعْرُوفَ إِلَى مَنْ هُوَ أَهْلُهُ
وَإِلَى مَنْ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِهِ
فَإِنْ أَصَبْتَ أَهْلَهُ فَهُوَ أَهْلُهُ
فَإِنْ لَمْ تُصِبْ أَهْلَهُ فَأَنْتَ مِنْ أَهْلِهِ
آفَةُ الْجُودِ السَّرَفُ
آفَةُ الْحَدِيثِ الْكَذِبُ
آفَةُ الْحَسَبِ الْفَخْرُ
آفَةُ الْحِلْمِ السَّفَهُ
آفَةُ السَّمَاحَةِ الْمَنُّ
آفَةُ الشَّجَاعَةِ الْبَغْيُ
آفَةُ الظَّرْفِ الصَّلَفُ
آفَةُ الْعِبَادَةِ الْفَتْرَةُ
آفَةُ الْعِلْمِ النِّسْيَانُ

الْتَمِسُوا الْجَارَ قَبْلَ شِرَاءِ الدَّارِ
وَالرَّفِيقَ قَبْلَ الطَّرِيقِ

إِمْلَاءُ الْخَيْرِ خَيْرٌ مِنَ السُّكُوتِ
وَالسُّكُوتُ خَيْرٌ مِنْ إِمْلَاءِ الشَّرِّ

إِنَّ أَكْثَرَ مَا يُدْخِلُ النَّاسَ الْجَنَّةَ
تَقْوَى اللهِ وَحُسْنُ الْخُلُقِ

إِنَّ الْحَسَدَ يَأْكُلُ الْحَسَنَاتِ
كَمَا تَأْكُلُ النَّارُ الْحَطَبَ

إِنَّ الْعَبْدَ لَيُدْرِكُ بِحُسْنِ الْخُلُقِ
دَرَجَةَ الصَّائِمِ الْقَائِمِ

إِنَّ اللهَ بِقِسْطِهِ وَعَدْلِهِ جَعَلَ الرَّوْحَ وَالْفَرَحَ
فِي الْيَقِينِ وَالرِّضَى
وَجَعَلَ الْهَمَّ وَالْحُزْنَ
فِي الشَّكِّ وَالسَّخَطِ

إِنَّ اللهَ يُعْطِي الدُّنْيَا عَلَى نِيَّةِ الْآخِرَةِ
وَيَأْبَى أَنْ يُعْطِيَ الْآخِرَةَ عَلَى نِيَّةِ الدُّنْيَا

إِنَّ قَلِيلَ الْعَمَلِ مَعَ الْعِلْمِ كَثِيرٌ
وَكَثِيرَ الْعَمَلِ مَعَ الْجَهْلِ قَلِيلٌ
